scope: SDevice-only stable three-factor decomposition of the electron SG transport response

factorization.qf_log_imbalance: log(left SG state term / right SG state term); with SimpleMOS variable-ni BGN and unclamped endpoint exponents this is (phin1-phin0)/Vt
factorization.sg_secant_conductance: positive logarithmic-mean SG state weight times Vt and finite-volume edge geometry, excluding mobility
factorization.mobility: complete Vela production edge mobility, including PhuMob, Enormal, HFS state and drive effects
factorization.allocation: exact three-factor Shapley value over all 8 binary subsets
factorization.endpoint_policy: independently evaluate production solved-equation electron-flux terms for the empty and full subsets
factorization.mixed_kernel_policy: evaluate the logarithmic-mean secant factor in boost cpp_dec_float_100 arithmetic

adjoint_weighting.node_weight: minus lambda_electron times the contact-eliminated electron continuity flux response

decision_questions: Does the stable secant decomposition remove the Bernoulli/population cancellation exposed by M16?
Is the M16 SG-state-kernel response controlled mainly by positive edge conductance or by quasi-Fermi imbalance?
Which spatial region carries the non-cancelled conductance and quasi-Fermi contributions?
Does the same dominant factor persist across all eight strong-inversion states?
interpretation_limits: The factors partition the Vela SG operator response and are not native Sentaurus residual terms.
The secant conductance contains coupled electrostatic, variable-ni, carrier-population and quasi-Fermi common-mode state effects.
The quasi-Fermi factor is an edge log-imbalance, not the HFS mobility driving-field discretization.
Sub-fA relative responses remain conditioning-sensitive and are not used for headline attribution.
